All positions on GBP/USd closed manually in profit. It has been taking too long to move and with the NY open coming up I will find better trades for my capital.

The message is not to get married to a trade and unless there is movement within a reasonable period of time, it means pro money are not behind it. This is not to say the move will eventually go in the direction I had chosen, but I want to see clearer signs of activity and commitment.

Cheers all.
Hey Doc, welcome back.

After I closed the trades we saw a nice false move up which cleared out all the shorts, took in new longs and the reversal in turn took out all the new longs giving more margin for pro money. On the close of that hourly candle I am short again and slowing loading up and will play this longer term because we have plenty room for profit to the down side.

S&P500 entering 4hr demand on an intraday test, will be watching this closely.

S&P500 moved up as envisaged and will likely continue to 1420 approx where a 4hr candle has a spike back in the recent past. I wont be taking this long until that spike is taken out and price returns back down to sit in that area and gain support for the real push up.

This could take days to play out, so dont spend your day watching the 5min chart waiting for that setup.

For the moment if I were long I would be happy to ride it up to 1419 for the NY close and be happy with the points earned.

Next week is setting up for a good bullish time on the S&P500 and as always we wait for the right entry point and jump in at a low risk area. Where the S&P500 can sting is in its deep pull backs, it likes to test your nerve of every move.
Good to have you back doc. Have a great week-end.

Welcome back Doctor:)

hope everything's ok and thanks as always for the charts and your time!

There wont any new charts from me for a few days, one of my 27 inch monitors went to silicon heaven and a replacement is on the way. I cannot trade will one less monitor and unless I have four in front of me no new trades will be placed. I am limping through managing the single GBP/USD short trade that has been running since last Friday.

I will have you all note that there will be very little activity expected in the NY session today because the floor will remain closed until tomorrow and only electronic trades placed. At least that was the information given to me last night.

With that in mind it is wise to concentrate on the London session and the GBP/USD trade I have in place is slowly paying dividends. It took a long time to fall over and there has been a nice clean break of an old decision area to the left....yes I too would like you show you a chart but its such a pain limping along with one eye less on the market. Given the decision area is broke and volume will be lighter there are two options open to anyone trading this pair. You either target the next close area of demand to the left which is where we are now, or wait to see will the 1hr candle close deep into this and watch for a pull back/failure following. I am playing this off the longer time frames because my early warning radar system is no longer stealthy enough to keep up with the lower time frames.

If you look on the 4hr chart you will see another old decision area to the left at around 1.6014. I wont bail at that price either, I am sticking to a lower price and into very clear and clean daily demand, which is a nice gathering of daily/4hr/1hr and lower demand. I expect to make lunch money out of this move. Also note we have major support below this daily demand area and a spike into it would give me a feel good factor for longs soon after.

Checking the monthly chart tells us the pro money look like they will take it higher, but before we see that happen they must gather more lower prices for best profit and that means stopping you out, getting you trading in the wrong direction and having a spike competition on the lower time frames. See how any shorts are relatively tight for profit margin on the higher time frames?....it makes sense to have a deep move down and then head for the highs of around 2.000, a great number and will concentrate many minds.

The monthly also shows you a retest of the original demand move, there are no more buyers left down that low and also note the clean support area even on the monthly. Please keep in mind that the year just gone is a tight range play. There has been little movement in any direction. When this comes about look for evidence of where it may move from the previous sensible price action. That was in 2008 and in late 2010.

I know you are screaming for a chart now, I feel your pain!

Looking on the weekly I see last weeks candle closed with plenty pain for the bears. It pushed well down into a lower time frame decision which had enough orders waiting to reverse the billions that were short and into bullish orders and closed above the previous weeks candle and resulted in a strong bullish engulfing candle.

When you look at it top down you see where the pro money is at work. You really do have to wait for at least the daily to setup before you can see a clear direction of where they are going. All the intra day time frames will chop you to bits unless you know where the support/resistance is and where the historical price areas of interest were.

money is not showing it is heavily short. If it were we would see better moves lower and without deep pull backs.

The 5min chart at this moment shows price atalled at......the old decision area. Who could have guessed?...but its stalled at the low end of the decision candle, that says its a weak stall and I hold for lower prices and more lunch money. The 1 hour has plenty untested demand below and all useful information for those who wish to hold the position longer.

We have a few hours before London closes and NY e trading opens.

Hi Simon,

In an ideal world the area you have in red lines or a little below would suit best, we know price has to fall before it rises in order for pro money to get a good margin and get in at the cheapest prices. There is one red spike down into the top of the red line you have on your chart, but I feel we need more down side than that. What is a cause for concern is the drift down rather than being pushed lower on the lower time frames. The daily is where you will see clear bullish engulfing and support. Getting into that engulfing candle will be helpful.

Also look at the bearish candle on the previous day, there is support back in price history to this. The change in sentiment, although early, can be seen in the large bullish candles a few days ago and these are the first strong bullish signs since August.

At the time of typing this, there is nice bearish rejection which gels with the down side move. London are currently finishing up their tea and crumpet for the day and NY opening. This may be one of the few times in the NY session where automated trading will become apparent and no other market noise to mask it.
Thanks for this Doctor. I've remarked my GU D1 chart as follows and will watch this pair closely in the coming days and weeks.

At present its now paying for next weeks lunch and perhaps next months if it keeps ticking lower. 1.5950 looks a good place for a target for those who took this earlier today and are still holding.

Next place to watch for a hiccup is 1.6014 area.

All time frames up to 4hr are strongly bearish at the moment. This is right into London close and watch for profit taking a pull back.

What I note is it reacted strongly off a 1 min time frame pull back which was a less than clear decision area on the 5min chart. What you see is a tail on a bearish candle and a wick on a bullish candle that closed bearish, strongly bearish.

I hope that last comment makes sense, if not think about it for a while.

We have lots of room to the down side and the last most significant candle, the 4 hr has closed strong with very little draw back. A good sign of pro money active.

Closing below near term over head resistance would be nice to see now, then a rest of that and failure.

I have been watching the GBP/USD pair all day waiting for failure. And its very slowly starting to unwind. Making this chart possible is my shiny new monitor and i feel one with the markets again:)

This is a 5min chart and not to be taken as trading advice or a reason to place a trade. What I want to show you here is how a market direction changes and what signs to look for. There is no 100% certainty that the market is changing now, but rather what signs tend to show up and what gives us reason to pay attention.

First off the blue line is support and resistance. I omitted by typical S/R comment as I see a lot of new people in here and its helpful to new people to get to terms with the buzz words us old farts throw around and not considering there are others who look at the screen and say....what?

Note the bullish break from the support line which is one of the most powerful things you can look for in trading. If you take longs off support and shorts off resistance you will do yourself a huge favor. What ties nicely into that is when support forms along side historic buying and resistance forming along side historic selling. Either one is a powerful combination and I have depended on this proven fact for a long time. Master one, then the other.

enough waffle, onto more charting. The bullish move off support has reached 4hr supply and we expect some reaction given it is the first test of this price area. What you cannot tell for sure is if there is enough reason for pro money to push up through old supply and absorb all the sellers, or just satisfy themselves they have enough profit to the long side and unwind their positions and look for the next move. Market timing for intraday trading like this is crucial for you to understand how it works. If you see a nice setup and its close to the market close, let it go. You only want to trade in an active market where pro money is also active.

Now that the 4hjr supply has been hit and the 4hr candle has closed on it lows, this is a good indication for further bearish activity, tomorrow, not now. You dont have the capital to trade this over night and have such a wide stop that any market spikes wont take you out. Make good use of your capital by trading it wisely and putting it to best use where you get profit within a reasonable period of time.

As price came back down it bounced off our blue line, pure price action. The move back up went nowhere and a sign of the bulls are about done. When price came down to the support line again, it blew right through and didnt look back for a long time. When it eventually came back it bounced back down proving to us that this area is an area of historic support and resistance and its giving us a trade entry....at some point in the future, or now if you have a trade plan in mind that works this early in.

A little more recent we got another small move up to the S/R line and off we bounce again.

Look at other time frames and note as price moved up all the little pull backs you see are a combination of profit taking and new orders, and the small fish bailing out. Always keep the over all market direction and its timing in the front of your mind so that you can at least recognise where the likely true reactions will be and not get suckered by all the low time frame noise and fake moves.

Tomorrow is Friday and a good day for a sell off. We have more room for margin/profit to the bearish side than we do for any bullish move. One thing I often ask of you is to use the logical side of your brain. If you had a billion dollars, would you be taking a long or short order around here?

The amount of capital you have is of no consequence, you treat the value of your money equal to those who have a lot more than you do. As you see the signs of active pro money at the areas I mentioned and with higher time frame support/demand and supply/resistance, you want to ride on the coat tails of the pro's.

For the moment I will continue to watch this pair and pull the bearish trigger when I feel the right opportunity presents itself and the lucky rabbits foot indicator is kicking me in the shins. Keep in mind, this is very early analysis, the market changes and we change with it and we are not blindly trading in a surprise direction.

Doc, thanks for answering my question earlier today and for the analysis above. There is not alot to ask because everything is explained very well, but after some thinking I have this question:

You have 1.6125 as an important price point and I also had this price on my chart. I have uploaded a chart, with a blue arrow poiting why I have this line on my chart, because of the hourly closes above this price. And after looking back (red arrows) it looks like it's indeed proven in the past. My question is if my view corresponds with your view for picking this price.

The daily and 4hr time frames are the more reliable times from which you ought to get price areas from. There is a lot of money changing hands around these 4hr + daily areas and it takes time for the pro money to close out all their positions and not move the market too much against themselves and eat into their profit, and potentially hurt the margin on a reverse i.e bearish sentiment taking over.

All sorts of tricks will come to play out in the form of false moves and even multi hour bullish moves that look strong. But pro money only enters the market when it has the best price and best position within the big picture. It is easy to loose sight of that when trading intra day.

Look at each area you see thats of interest being an 'area' and not a line, price wont always turn on a dime. The biggest reason for me not to short this yet is on the daily you will see we are hovering above a major bearish sell off area. If the bulls want to retain control they have a lot of buying to do and not much in the way of a clear over head target. The weekly time frame shows a series of tighter range bound trading and until we see a break and retest of either direction, there wont be very good moves. A small chunk of a clear intra day target would suit me for the moment.

So Doc, I am watching the eur in the asian session and bam for no apparent reason the things is headed south hard. I understand your bias has been bearish but no serious level has been hit.

Is this a big indication that pro money is selling and front running the news? It is non farm payroll on the fx calendar so I got this feeling that someone is front running the news and accidentally put a little too much sell position on the table trying to front run everyone in the asia session. Just some fun plot I played out in my head.

Some guy with alot of money going 'oops'.

The pair I am watching is the GBP/USD and not the Euro.

The EUR/USD is heading for the bottom of a price range where it has been unable to break out of for a long time now. The boas on that pair at the bottom of the range, and if it holds, is till bullish. I would not trade it lower unless there is reason to do so, but I would take it higher if I see activity by pro money to the long side.

The Euro has come off monthly lows which are highly significant and it rallied quickly up into supply, the reaction at supply was a weak and short move down and this is where price has formed a small range. There are no clear signals on the Euro yet to it. So we wait again and if you are really keen, take a look at any time frame of the Euro. Do you see the amount of time it spends in consolidation vs trend?

There is approximate 75% of the time in consolidation and 25% trending. But the classic analysis of trend means you miss most of the moves. The books are all telling people to trade at the wrong time.

Look at longer time frames and see where does it make most logical sense for obvious room for profit. Pro money are rarely wrong and dont change directions at the flick of a switch either.

A small update.

We now have over head resistance on the GBP/USD pair on the 5min, 15min 30min and 60min time frames. The last 1hr candle shows a clear sign of bears coming in and minor retests on the 5min chart shows me we have active pro money. There are price areas within the 5min chart getting hit virtually to the point and price reacting off. This may look chaotic but it is highly ordered and 'routine'.

Another piece of the puzzle is a heads up on the 1hr time frame that reached old demand, this has been ignored, partially due to it getting spiked on the 31st of last month (look for hourly candle spike) and all the butyers are no longer there and what I am looking for now is a break lower and positioning being done right now by pro money who are loading up for the move.

I remain bearish on this pair and will wait for higher prices to scale in to the down side. A fake move up or maybe a few nice large spikes should shake out the weak holders and clear the path. Unless the over head resistance is broken there is good potential on this pair.

fxfury, I look at each pair on their own rather than seek confluence or agreement from one other pair. The concept of confluence falls over just as sloping lines do, eventually all fail because price is not always going to adhere strictly to what a human reads into both confluence and price vectors. Neither has been proven to be reliable over time.....and the most important thing you will read today is....price is not a vector!.....it does not have any clue what an indicator or a sloping line means. Pro money trade to price areas and a price area is not something you can find reliably with any indicator.

Take each pair on their own and if you are looking to short the Euro, by all means make sure it is indeed weak by looking at ALL the other pairs traded against it. The same principle applies to all currencies.

@mel, I like your charts and analysis very tight and concise. If we pull back the bullish move will come to an end because we would be getting too far against pro money's acceptable price areas from where they are positioned. They often trade against themselves and will turn the market with buy backs when enough of the herd are also in on the apparent main move.

We are certainly heading lower on the Euro today and will look for next nearest support. I am loaded up on GBP and concentrating on more lunch money from that today.
